prompt.brief: Design a hotel reservation platform that searches location and date availability, holds rooms, accepts payment, confirms bookings, and prevents double booking across channels.
successSignals: Model room inventory by property, room type, date, rate plan, and hold/booking state rather than caching a single availability number.
Use a short-lived hold and conditional inventory transaction before payment capture, with an explicit expiry and recovery path.
Make confirmation, cancellation, payment callbacks, and partner-channel retries idempotent and auditable.
Explain overbooking policy, timezone boundaries, stale search results, refunds, inventory reconciliation, and fraud controls.

functional: Search properties and rates by location and dates, inspect policies, place a temporary hold, pay, and confirm a reservation.
Support cancellations, modifications, refunds, partner inventory updates, guest identity, and booking notifications.
Expose availability freshness, hold expiry, payment state, confirmation code, inventory audit, and reconciliation status.
nonFunctional: Never oversell a room inventory unit unless an explicit property overbooking policy permits it.
Handle high concurrency by partitioning inventory by property and date and isolating popular hotels and event dates.
Make holds, payment authorization, confirmation, cancellation, and partner callbacks idempotent.
Return a pending payment or unavailable state rather than confirming when inventory or processor state is uncertain.
scaleAssumptions: Search 10 million properties and process 100,000 booking attempts per minute during travel and event peaks.
Partition by property, room type, and stay date; isolate hot properties and aggregate search caches separately.
Retain inventory ledgers, holds, payments, confirmations, partner messages, and reconciliation evidence.

architecture.title: Hotel Booking System domain architecture
architecture.summary: Design a hotel reservation platform that searches location and date availability, holds rooms, accepts payment, confirms bookings, and prevents double booking across channels. The design makes hotel booking system decisions durable, isolates slow or external work behind replayable boundaries, and exposes freshness, authorization, and recovery state to operators and clients.

layers.label: Booking reliability operations

deepDives.title: Inventory claims and oversell control
points: Use conditional writes or a serialized inventory partition for hotel booking system scarce capacity.
Give holds an expiry and reaper, but never release a confirmed claim from a stale worker.
Separate searchable availability from the authoritative claim path.

deepDives.title: Payment and unknown outcomes
points: Bind hotel booking system payment attempts to the intent and request hash, not just the customer session.
Treat timeout as unknown, query or reconcile provider state, and avoid a blind second charge.
Keep sensitive payment tokens outside business records and logs.

deepDives.title: Fulfillment and partner recovery
points: Publish hotel booking system events after commit, consume at least once, and track per-stage progress.
Use reconciliation against partner feeds or delivery evidence instead of assuming a callback arrives.
Expose pending and expired status so the client can explain what happened.

tradeoffs.title: Reservation versus oversell tolerance
tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer a short-lived hotel booking system claim for scarce inventory and state the consistency scope explicitly.
tradeoffs.caution: A cache or search index cannot safely decrement the final room count.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous checkout versus asynchronous fulfillment
tradeoffs.recommendation: Commit the reservation intent synchronously and move partner or delivery work behind events.
tradeoffs.caution: Waiting for downstream fulfillment makes retries ambiguous and increases checkout tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Precompute availability versus compute at read time
tradeoffs.recommendation: Precompute common search dimensions but validate the final claim against authoritative state.
tradeoffs.caution: Serving only a precomputed hotel booking system availability view creates oversell or stale-price failures.

commonMistakes: Charging before a hotel booking system inventory claim is durable.
Retrying a timed-out payment without resolving the first attempt.
Letting stale search results act as the final availability decision.
Making cancellation and hold expiry non-idempotent.
Failing to reconcile late partner confirmations, refunds, or delivery failures.

followUps.question: How do you avoid double reservations?
followUps.answer: Persist the hotel booking system request idempotency key, condition the intent transition, and make inventory, payment, and fulfillment consumers deduplicate the same command.

followUps.question: What if inventory changes between search and checkout?
followUps.answer: Recheck authoritative availability, return an explicit unavailable or repriced result, and do not silently convert a failed claim into a confirmed one.

followUps.question: How do you repair a stuck fulfillment?
followUps.answer: Use an operation timeline, provider evidence, retry-safe transitions, and an operator-approved compensating action or cancellation.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the hotel booking system workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative hotel booking system state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions hotel booking system traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the hotel booking system user experience.
